page: Microsoft Azure D64_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the Dv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Additionally, the instance includes 1638 GB of local storage, while containing no integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance profiles. Single-core execution, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25% tier, reflecting the older architecture and moderate clock speed of the Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by Passmark CPU and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tests. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached operations remains in the middle 50% tier, supporting steady data throughput. Large-model LLM text generation performs poorly, landing in the bottom 10%, though prompt processing for small and medium models achieves average speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64_v3 offers a high density of legacy vCPUs and memory resources, making it a viable option for workloads that benefit from parallel execution without requiring state-of-the-art single-thread performance. The bundled 1638 GB of local storage enhances its utility for data-intensive tasks. This server is suited for general-purpose enterprise applications, multi-threaded database operations, static web serving, and software compilation tasks.
